thinking_and_logic: You began with a brute-force nested-loop approach and correctly sensed it would be too slow. With guidance, you shifted to the standard complement lookup technique: iterate once, compute complement = target - n, check if it was previously seen (and if so return indices), otherwise store n -> i for future matches. This reasoning aligns with the canonical optimal approach and correctly avoids reusing the same element by checking before inserting.
code_assessment: Your final code matches the answer key’s optimal solution (single pass hash map). Compared to the brute-force canonical baseline, your approach achieves O(n) time by replacing the inner loop with O(1) average hash lookups; compared to common pitfalls, you avoided using the same element twice by checking the complement before writing the current index, and the dictionary mapping supports duplicates correctly. The only notable gap is not documenting behavior for impossible cases (though constraints guarantee a solution).
